$comment: Command guard for factory agents (PreToolUse on Bash), implemented in lib/factory_core/guard.py. The guard tokenises the command like a shell (compound commands, $(...), bash -c, eval, heredocs, wrappers such as env/sudo/xargs/npx, global options) and runs tool checks on every simple command; rules with a pattern are bounded regexes searched in the whole text. deny = blocked with the reason; ask = Claude Code asks the human; deny wins. You may change a rule's decision here. Defence in depth on top of Claude Code permissions, not a sandbox.

rules.reason: The factory never pushes. Commit on the job branch; the human decides what to push.
Merging, opening PRs, releasing, running workflows or changing secrets on GitHub is a human decision.
This GitHub API call changes something on GitHub.
This changes issues, pull requests or repositories on GitHub.
Publishing packages, images, charts or releases is a human decision.
This changes a package registry account or package.
The factory never applies or mutates infrastructure state. It writes code and runs fmt/validate/plan; a human applies after approval.
The factory never deploys. A human deploys after approval.
This cloud CLI call can change cloud resources or data.
This changes a Kubernetes cluster. Confirm it targets a disposable local cluster.
This changes a Kubernetes cluster through Helm.
Recursive delete of a root, home, parent, system or wildcard path is never allowed.
Recursive permission changes on root, home or system folders are never allowed.
Disk formatting and raw device writes are never allowed.
This runs a command as root.
This runs a script that arrives through a pipe (for example curl … | sh).
This inline program mentions a push, publish, deploy or the factory's own state.
This runs a command whose name is in a variable, with a verb like push, deploy or delete.
This runs commands on another machine.
This changes git configuration that runs programs, defines aliases or reaches remotes.
This changes the user's global git configuration.
Factory agents change code only in the job's worktree; the main checkout belongs to the user. Start the command with cd <Worktree> &&.
Agents never touch the factory's own state (job.json, messages, entries, config, factoryctl); only their Output file.
The guard could not check this command (too long, too deeply nested or unbalanced quotes), so a human should look at it.
Fork bombs are never allowed.
This drops, truncates or empties data. Confirm the target is a disposable local database.
This looks like it targets production.
This runs migrations against an explicitly configured, non-local database URL.
This reads a credential file. Agents must not read or print secrets.
Agents never touch the factory's own state (job.json, messages, entries, config, factoryctl); only their Output file.
Git hooks run on the user's machine outside any job; agents never change them.
This touches the repository's shared git configuration.
